title: Invocation broker playbook: harmonize OpenAI-style tools with legacy function surfaces
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Problem: Customers call Redwood APIs with two primary invocation styles: OpenAI-style 'tools' (JSON schemas, named tool objects, streaming toolcall events) and our older 'legacy function' surface (positional/typed params, non-streaming). These diverge on naming conventions, parameter encoding, streaming semantics (partial tool output events vs final function-return), and output typing (structured JSON vs opaque string). This ticket defines an invocation broker and compatibility playbook that lets the runtime accept either surface and reliably route, normalize, and emit interoperable telemetry while minimizing client-breaking behavior.

Goals:
- Single canonical invocation path inside the runtime (Invocation Broker) that accepts multiple client shapes.
- Deterministic name resolution and parameter mapping with explicit fallback rules.
- Streaming envelope that preserves structured output and toolcall progress across both surfaces.
- Safe rollout strategy with feature flags and telemetry to detect regressions.

Non-goals: Full language-level shim for every historical SDK (that will be separate follow-ups).
acceptance_criteria: Invocation Broker accepts OpenAI tool calls and legacy function calls and normalizes to a single internal event schema.
Name resolution table implemented: exact match -> canonical name -> alias fallback -> fuzzy-match logged for later backfill.
Parameter mapping supports positional->named translations, simple type coercion (string->int if safe), and rejects ambiguous cases with clear error messages.
Streaming semantics: partial tool outputs emitted as 'tool.stream' events and final result as 'tool.exec.result' across both client surfaces.
No more than 5% increase in 95th percentile per-invocation latency in synthetic benchmarks during brokerized path (smoke test).
E2E tests cover: tool name aliasing, parameter coercion, streaming events ordering, error fallthrough to fallback model, and telemetry tags for routing decisions.
updates: 2025-02-14 - Discovery: interviewed 4 PMs and 6 SDK maintainers. Common pain: inconsistent tool names across integrations; customers want graceful backcompat when renaming. Decided to implement an alias registry and metrics for fuzzy resolution.

2025-02-20 - Prototype: created inv-broker PoC that normalizes OpenAI tool call JSON to internal schema and emits streaming envelopes. PoC pushed to branch feature/invocation-broker-poc. See PR link in 'links'.

2025-02-25 - Design review with runtime and API teams. Key decisions: (1) use prioritized name resolution (exact -> canonical -> alias -> fuzzy) with explicit telemetry on each hop, (2) require explicit opt-in for automatic type coercion, (3) stream envelopes must include provenance header (client_surface, tool_name_original).
2025-02-28 - Security review kickoff: sharing data flow diagrams with Security for KMS/HSM impact (no secrets stored, only names/params). Security requested threat model doc; assigned to EngSec.

2025-03-03 - Telemetry smoke: instrumented PoC with lightweight metrics. Observed median broker overhead ~1.4ms and p95 increase ~3.2ms on synthetic microbench. Marking initial performance acceptable for canary rollout.
2025-03-04 - PR opened for runtime integration: GH PR #8214. Requesting design sign-off from API owners and SDK leads before canary. Added rollout plan below.
rollout_plan: Phase 1: deploy broker behind feature-flag to 10% traffic for internal orgs, collect telemetry for name-resolution hops and latency for 48h. Phase 2: expand to 50% and enable alias backfill job for fuzzy matches. Phase 3: enable for all traffic and flip SDKs to default canonical naming rules. Each phase gated by automated healthchecks and abort window.
testing_plan: Unit tests for name-resolution table and param coercion. Integration tests simulate OpenAI tool stream events and legacy function returns with random alias sets. Gateway load test simulating 5k req/s for 10 minutes and compare latency with/without broker. Add contract tests to SDK CI verifying deterministic streaming event ordering.
implementation_notes: Key components: (1) NameResolver service with in-memory cache and periodic alias backfill job, (2) ParamTranslator module with configurable coercion rules, (3) StreamEnvelope abstraction added to transport layer, (4) Telemetry hooks for resolution path, fallback reason, and latency. Keep modules pluggable for Dedicated/Private deployments where customers may want custom alias registries.
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: fuzzy-match false positives could route to wrong tool. Mitigation: log fuzzy matches and don't auto-resolve until operator-approved alias added; in the meantime return a helpful 409 with candidate list. Risk: streaming ordering regressions. Mitigation: enforce per-invocation monotonic sequence IDs in envelopes and add e2e tests.
review_notes: API owners (Liam O'Connell) requested stricter error schema for ambiguous parameter coercion. SDK lead (Nina Rodriguez) recommended an opt-in flag in SDKs to enable legacy coercion behavior. Added to acceptance criteria and testing_plan.
next_steps: 1) Address Security threat model comments (due 2025-03-07). 2) Iterate on PR #8214 per code review. 3) Prepare canary config and monitor playbook. 4) Create customer-facing compatibility doc for support and account teams.
